---
title: "Curves, holes and transforms"
description: "Preserve the declared boundary shape and placement through native modeling."
sidebar: simulation
---

The requested conductor boundary must reach the native model with its hole
topology, curve meaning and placement intact. A smooth picture is not a
replacement for the declared geometry.

## Input supplied by OrPen

- Positive metal outer rings and explicit nonmetal holes.
- Authored line/arc/spline laws, parameters and trims when selected.
- Polygon-only input and the exact selected edge chain when reconstruction is requested.
- Source units and actual rotation/reflection/translation.
- Port anchors, normals and directed lines in their owning source frame.

Interpolation through-points are not B-spline control points. OrPen's Hermite
strip definition must not be treated as equivalent to another interpolation
law merely because both pass through the same points.

## Backend requirements

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

| Workflow stage | Required delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Boundary construction | Build the requested CAD edges/faces and hole loops for the selected Route A/B model. |
| Reconstruction | Replace only the explicitly selected polygon chain; retain other edges and source attribution. |
| Placement | Transform geometry, curve directions and ports once; retain reflected orientation. |
| Discretization | Keep CAD shape, geometric mesh order and FEM order distinguishable. |

### AEDT

| Workflow stage | Required delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Boundary construction | Build native conductor contours with preserved holes and declared curve/approximation meaning. |
| Reconstruction | Honor the same explicit reconstruction choice if used; do not silently fit a new contour. |
| Placement | Transform bodies/supports and port directions consistently, with source-to-native coordinates. |
| Discretization | Keep source shape and native geometry separate from adaptive mesh approximation. |

:::

If the requested shape cannot be represented, return that fact; do not report
success after an undisclosed polygonal or lower-order replacement. This is a
required output/failure behavior, not a record of current implementation.

## Final product to inspect

Native boundary views and source-linked edge/loop records, including holes,
endpoints, trims and transformed port directions. For higher-order mesh
curvature, include representative coordinates/connectivity; degree labels alone
do not prove curved geometry.

Candidates: disk/annulus for holes and circles; arc/interpolation/B-spline
strips for distinct curve laws; explicitly placed variants for transforms.
[Inspect these sources](../../public-pdk-examples/test-components.md).

::: {.callout-note title="Inspect the declared shape first"}

[Curves, holes and transforms](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/GeometrySemantics/geometry_curves_holes_transforms.ipynb)
keeps the source contour, curve declaration and actual placed reference
together. Use it to identify the requested boundary before examining the
backend's native edges/loops. Compare the annulus hole, strip endpoints and
transformed port anchors, rather than comparing only silhouettes.

:::

A sheet normal describes its plane orientation; a directed integration or
current line describes the selected in-plane direction. Both must follow the
authored placement without being substituted for each other.

Serves [capacitance](../requirements/electrostatic-capacitance.qmd),
[eigenmode](../requirements/eigenmode.qmd), [EPR](../requirements/epr-loss.qmd)
and [driven modal](../requirements/driven-modal.qmd).
